assembly_manifest.title: All-In with Chamath, Jason, Sacks & Friedberg — On-device inference and task-specific small language models
Excess Returns — Small-cap value, valuation mean reversion, and the AI capital cycle
Masters of Scale — AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and frontier-model release restraint
Dwarkesh Podcast — Intel’s EUV adoption lag and maturity gates for new manufacturing technologies

narration_plan.speaker: A
narration_plan.text: Today on The Daily Rundown: smaller AI models, the price of the AI boom, and vulnerability discovery.

narration_plan.speaker: B
narration_plan.text: Plus, Intel’s chipmaking gamble—and the cost of waiting for new technology.

narration_plan.speaker: A
narration_plan.text: On All-In, a discussion featuring IBM’s Arvind Krishna and Palo Alto Networks’ Nikesh Arora explores small, task-specific models and on-device AI. The practical question: how do companies move from trying AI to actually using it?

narration_plan.speaker: B
narration_plan.text: On Excess Returns, Rob Arnott says the largest 500 stocks went from a discount to smaller peers to an 80 percent premium. His AI capital-cycle discussion asks where investors are paying too much for growth.

narration_plan.speaker: B
narration_plan.text: On Masters of Scale, OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar describes AI-discovered PHP vulnerabilities and coordinated disclosure. With today’s reporting cautioning there’s no easy exploit, this connects model-release decisions to real-world security.

narration_plan.speaker: A
narration_plan.text: On the Dwarkesh Podcast, a chipmaking discussion examines why Intel delayed extreme-ultraviolet lithography while TSMC adopted it earlier. It’s a consequential timing problem: when is new manufacturing technology ready to bet on?

narration_plan.speaker: B
narration_plan.text: That’s The Daily Rundown. Thanks for listening.
